title: Advancing Biological Electron Microscopy: Innovative 3D-Printed Solutions for Automated Sample Processing
content: Preparing biological samples for transmission electron microscopy (TEM) is a complex and labor-intensive process that often involves hazardous chemicals and frequent reagent exchanges. Although automated sample processors have reduced manual handling and minimized human exposure, most commercially available systems are primarily designed for tissue samples, limiting their applicability to other biological specimen types. Recent systems have been developed to accommodate monolayer cell cultures or small-scale samples [1], but these devices often feature complex designs, are optimized for large-batch processing, and are cost-prohibitive for many research core facilities.
